question.problem:
Suppose that $L$ is a linear differential operator such that $L({y}_{1})=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x$ and $L({y}_{2})=6{sin}^{2}⁡x$ for some functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x).$ What is $L(3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})?$

*Hint: Use $\operatorname{cos}⁡2x={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x.$*
question.worked_solution:
For any linear differential operator,

$$
L(a{y}_{1}(x)+b{y}_{2}(x))=aL({y}_{1}(x))+bL({y}_{2}(x))
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants. 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L(3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}) & =3L({y}_{1})+L({y}_{2}) \\  & =3\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡2x+6{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =3({cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x)+6{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =3{cos}^{2}⁡x-3{sin}^{2}⁡x+6{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =3({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
